prompt: Our background-worker fleet processes jobs off a queue and uses a Redlock-style distributed lock — N independent Redis nodes, quorum, a TTL, and a fencing token — to make sure two workers never touch the same job at once. The safety machinery checks out on paper, but throughput is way below what N workers should give us: with N=5 workers running, monitoring shows jobs completing at roughly the rate of ONE worker, and per-node timeout metrics show most of each lock's TTL getting eaten before the job even starts. Walk me through this code out loud — what's actually causing the serialization and the shrinking safety margin — and tell me how you'd optimize it for real throughput without weakening any of the lock's safety guarantees.
